question: How should Muslims who differ over eating non-zabihah meat treat each other?
answer:
So to conclude, dear brothers and sisters: this is a legitimate controversy. I personally follow the position of Ibn Taymiyyah and the Hanbali school and the Hanafi school in this regard. For those that follow the other position, no problem. If you're a Maliki, you're a Shafi'i, you have the right to do so. But all that I say is: look beyond the Bismillah issue, and think also of the Kitabi issue, and think also of the mechanism of slaughter.

And you know what? Isn't it pure and better to eat good food? Don't we want to be the person who feeds only pure? We don't want to be the one who raises his hands to Allah, as our Prophet ﷺ said, while he's eating haram and drinking haram and whatnot. So why take that risk? Even if you follow the school (and I'm saying you have the right to follow it), isn't it better to raise the bar, and to support your Muslim brothers and sisters and the halal businesses, and to try to feed your family that which is pure? I mean, even if it's halal according to the Shafi'i school, they would say it is better to eat the meat over which Allah's name has been mentioned. So strive to be better in this regard.

And at the end of the day, dear brothers and sisters, we should not make a big issue about this. I have good friends that eat non-zabihah meat, and I'll be very frank here. (I keep on saying this is the last thing; okay, inshallah, this is the last thing.) A very, very good friend of mine (I've known him from the Madinah days; mashaAllah, we are one of the tightest, 25 years almost) is now a shaykh, and he's a Shafi'i, a complete Shafi'i. And he eats only chicken and not beef. Why? Because of the slaughtering issue, because of the stunning issue. He says beef is a problem because too many animals die, and chicken, we know it's not going to die. And he doesn't believe the basmalah is wajib. And you know what? That's fine. He's Shafi'i, and he sticks with his usul; he's being fair. He eats chicken only in certain states, like Dallas, or, you know, Texas and whatnot, which I understand.

I want to tell you an anecdote, and with this we conclude, inshallah, to show you that we need to be more open-minded about this. I believe that that chicken is haram. I would never eat it. And I have never, inshallah, to the best of my knowledge, intentionally eaten non-zabihah since I came of age. So we went out to a restaurant. I ordered the fish; he ordered the chicken. And we're joking and whatnot. When it came time to pay the bill, I did a trick: I went out pretending to go to the bathroom and gave my Visa card, whatever. So I paid the bill. And he's like, "How could you pay? You think this is not even allowed." I said, "It's not allowed for me; it's allowed for you. Don't worry, I'm going to pay for it." I expected Allah to reward me for paying for the food. To be brutally honest, if I ate it, I might expect Allah's punishment. But I did not at all consider my dear brother in Islam to be doing anything wrong, because he's following his madhhab and he's following his 'ulama. That food on his plate, I would never touch it; that's my position. But he's eating it, and according to his paradigm and his usul and his madhhab, it is permissible. Alhamdulillah, good for him. And from my paradigm and madhhab, I don't think it's permissible.

You're going to break up your friendship because somebody's eating non-zabihah meat? Come on, please. This is a legitimate position. Imam al-Shafi'i held it. And if the brother is being consistent in the madhhab (which he is, by the way; he's not picking and choosing; he is a Shafi'i), what are you going to do? Alhamdulillah, no big deal. Live and let live, and don't make this an issue of making or breaking the bonds or whatnot. Alhamdulillah, this is a position from the beginning of Islam. **The position I follow is the majority one, and inshallah it is the correct one. But the other position also has its own paradigm and its own validity.** We ask Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala to guide all of us. And with this very, very long talk, I have become hungry. I'm going to go get some dessert, because the main course is over.
